output.summary: A cereal hybrid of wheat and rye, first bred in laboratories in late-19th-century Scotland and Germany. It combines wheat's yield and grain quality with rye's tolerance of disease and difficult growing conditions. Although grown mainly for animal feed, its grain is also used in some breakfast cereals and other foods.
output.edibilityNote: The grain is used less often for human food than animal feed; products include breakfast cereals and foods sold in health-food shops.
